new_statements.quote: 4-1. Le mancagne n'est pas une langue à tons. L'accent d'intensité domine la prosodie mancagne. Il est caractérisé par les traits suivants : a) il n'est pas distinctif ; b) sa place est prévisible ; c) il est susceptible d'engendrer l'allongement du centre de syllabe qui le supporte ; d) par la place qui lui est dévolue dans le lexème, il peut servir de signe démarcatif. À côté de l'accent principal, la langue use d'un accent secondaire.
new_statements.translation: 4-1. Mankanya is not a tone language. Intensity (stress) accent dominates Mankanya prosody. It is characterised by the following features: a) it is not distinctive; b) its place is predictable; c) it can bring about lengthening of the nucleus of the syllable that carries it; d) through the place assigned to it within the lexeme, it can serve as a demarcative sign. Beside the main accent, the language uses a secondary accent.

new_statements.relation_note: Catalog has Mankanya with an EMPTY rule and no existing statements; this adds: not a tone language, stress non-distinctive and predictable, demarcative within the lexeme, secondary stress present, stressed nucleus may lengthen. Access note: the listed open_url (rosettaproject_knf_vertxt-1) is only the Annexe of glossed texts, pp. 149-201, with no phonology; the sibling Rosetta item rosettaproject_knf_phon-1 (same book) holds pp. 11, 35-39, 51 and 53 and was used for the quote. p. 52 (§4-2, the placement rule and secondary accent) is in neither excerpt; the full book is at Harvard Tozzer (offsite, AFR.SUDAN T 733 m) if the placement sentence is wanted verbatim.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Non-tonal; a non-contrastive, predictable dynamic (intensity) stress with a fixed position inside the lexeme that marks lexeme boundaries; the stressed nucleus may lengthen. The sentence that actually names the position (§4-2, p. 52) is NOT in the open copy: the Rosetta excerpt jumps from p. 51 to p. 53. The root-initial reading is inferred from 'la place qui lui est dévolue dans le lexème' plus the two later sources (Gaved 2020, Creissels 2026) that summarise Trifkovič and place the accent on the first syllable of the root/lexical base; it is not quoted from Trifkovič's own pages.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Stated to exist ('la langue use d'un accent secondaire', p. 51); its placement is on the missing p. 52 and could not be read.
new_statements.exceptions: None in the open pages. p. 53 adds that intonation ('la hauteur mélodique') has no functional value and belongs to the utterance, not the word.
new_statements.identity_note: Trifkovič 1969 describes Mankanya (mancagne) as spoken in Casamance, Senegal (IFAN, Dakar; texts in the Annexe); Gaved 2020 covers Mankanya of Guinea-Bissau, Senegal and the Gambia; Creissels 2026 draws on Trifkovič, Gaved and Kanfome 2016 (parler mancagne de Goudomp). No source distinguishes dialects for the stress rule.

new_statements.quote: 2.10 Accent. Normally the accent is placed on the first syllable of the root. 2.11 Tone. Mankanya is not a tonal language. Some informants say that there is a grammatical difference in some sentences which are segmentally identical, which they say is tonal. However, my limited data on this does not corroborate this claim. [p. 29] — It is difficult to find true contrasts between [Pᵊ] and [Pə], because [Pᵊ] is normally found at the beginning of words and unstressed. [Pə] can be found initially in some inflected words, but it is then also stem initial and stressed. [p. 12]

new_statements.relation_note: Fills the catalog's empty rule with an explicit placement (root-initial). Consistent with Trifkovič 1969 (non-tonal, predictable demarcative stress within the lexeme). Included beyond the listed works because it is the modern reference grammar, open access at the publisher, and the only opened source that states the placement in English.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the first syllable of the root; noun-class and verbal prefixes (e.g. ʊ-, kɐ-, pə-) are unstressed, so the stressed syllable is the first or second syllable of the word depending on whether a prefix is present (examples ʊˈʂɐl, kɐˈtoh, nɐˈme, ʊˈko, p. 29). Not tonal.
new_statements.exceptions: 'Normally' hedges the rule; no listed exceptions. Unstressed /ə/ has a very short pre-accentual realisation and can be deleted in unstressed positions (pp. 12, 25). Some informants report tonal minimal pairs at sentence level; author's data do not confirm this (p. 29).
new_statements.identity_note: Trifkovič 1969 describes Mankanya (mancagne) as spoken in Casamance, Senegal (IFAN, Dakar; texts in the Annexe); Gaved 2020 covers Mankanya of Guinea-Bissau, Senegal and the Gambia; Creissels 2026 draws on Trifkovič, Gaved and Kanfome 2016 (parler mancagne de Goudomp). No source distinguishes dialects for the stress rule.

new_statements.quote: Le mankanya n'a pas de système tonal mais possède un accent de mot qui marque en règle générale la première syllabe de la base lexicale du mot (c'est-à-dire pratiquement la première ou la deuxième syllabe du mot, selon sa structure morphologique). [p. 2] — On note par ailleurs une tendance à la réduction de [ə] en syllabe initiale non accentuée, et ce [ə] réduit, bien que perceptible, n'est pas noté dans l'orthographe, d'où des graphies comme bkow 'tête' pour [bəkow]. [p. 1]
new_statements.translation: Mankanya has no tone system but has a word accent which as a general rule marks the first syllable of the lexical base of the word (that is, in practice the first or the second syllable of the word, depending on its morphological structure). — One also notes a tendency for [ə] to be reduced in an unaccented initial syllable, and this reduced [ə], although perceptible, is not written in the orthography, hence spellings like bkow 'head' for [bəkow].

new_statements.rule_in_words: No tone; word stress on the first syllable of the lexical base (stem-initial), which is the first or second syllable of the word depending on whether a prefix precedes the base; the unstressed prefix vowel ə reduces.

audit.reasoning: The deciding quotation is verbatim in the held LOT fulltext at the stated places (sec. 2.10 p. 29; sec. 2.2.3 pp. 11-12; sec. 2.9 p. 29). The source is the 2020 reference grammar, the newest and fullest description Glottolog lists; the transcribed examples throughout ch. 2 independently show unstressed C(ə)-/V- prefixes and root-initial stress, matching the 'morphological (root-initial)' coding. A newly downloaded 2026 phonology sheet by Creissels (Atlantic specialist) states the same rule ('accent de mot.. première syllabe de la base lexicale') and no tone. No instrumental or dedicated prosody study was found. Trifkovič 1969 (print-only) could add detail on exceptions behind Gaved's 'Normally' but nothing seen suggests a different coding.
